findings.title: Comment-separated subscript writes become plain evidence
findings.detail: A quoted reserved subscript key followed by a trailing comment and newline before the closing bracket is a valid static assignment target. Both classifiers return None for evidence and reencoding keys, including typed and augmented writes. A comment between the closing bracket and the closing parenthesis of a parenthesized assignment target also evades recognition. AST parsing and literal target inspection establish the writes without executing input. Five bounded defect variants classify plain in all eight UTF encoding views and plain/gzip/XZ recovery; 225 actual bound reads accept their bytes losslessly across UTF8/16/32 and five suffixes. This violates the actual-metadata-before-read boundary; no full task PASS forgery is asserted. S6 adjacent-prefix/comment keys, S7 named ASCII escapes and S8 multiline typed identifiers now reject in reviewed forms.

Preserve ordinary commented reader expressions, quoted values and separate annotations; add shared plain/recovery/history/suffix coverage and obtain fresh exact-revision review.
